html:
SMTO-EXE-0129 — SMTO got a reply from the web browser it couldn't trust

GUID: 625a7685-681d-57de-9d50-0d34caa864eb
Slug: browser-invalid-response
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO asked the web browser on your Gateway to do something, but the reply came back in a form SMTO couldn't check. If the step was a click, typing or a form submission, it may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to look at the current page and tell you what it shows, before it does anything else. A fresh look shows whether the click, typing or form submission already went through even though the reply was unreadable.
  2. If the page shows the step is done, carry on from there. Only ask SMTO to repeat it if the page clearly shows it didn't happen. Repeating a step that already worked could submit a form, send a message or place an order twice.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway this conversation uses. The Gateway is the helper program that runs the web browser. A Gateway that is out of date or misbehaving can send replies SMTO can't read, and the check shows its current state.

What success looks like

  • SMTO describes the current page normally, and new browser steps finish without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name and the website you were using, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to repeat a payment, purchase or form submission until you've checked on the website that it didn't go through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's browser result failed transport decoding or validate_response (closed response model, size limit or execution-status fields), so completion is not proven; for non-read operations the effect is marked unknown.

What this means

  • The Gateway result failed the browser's typed response contract or transport decoding; no valid receipt establishes completion from that response alone. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway result failed the browser's typed response contract or transport decoding; no valid receipt establishes completion from that response alone.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect receipt structure, original action and effect certainty, then reconcile same-session state before a repeat.

How to fix it

  • Compare the Server and Gateway versions (GatewayClient.browser_operation in src/agent_runtime/execution/gateway_client.py against validate_response in src/gateway_core/browser/contract.py) and check the Gateway log for the response it sent. Before repeating any mutating operation, read the current state with browser.page_info, browser.snapshot or browser.downloads, because an invalid response does not prove the operation did not run.
  • Refresh the selected Gateway and inspect the page before repeating mutations; an invalid response does not prove non-execution.

Retry and execution caution

  • Refresh the selected Gateway and inspect the page before repeating mutations; an invalid response does not prove non-execution.

How to verify the fix

  • The original outcome is established and future responses validate under the matching browser protocol.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
